items.title: In a two-dimensional Noetherian local ring an element avoiding the minimal primes extends to a system of parameters stable under small perturbations
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra)
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a Noetherian local ring (R, m) of dimension two and an element f in m contained in no minimal prime of R, and asserts the existence of g in m and an integer N such that f and g form a system of parameters and such that for every h in m^N, the pair f + h and g again forms a system of parameters with length_R(R/(f, g)) = length_R(R/(f + h, g)) (source lines 38107-38119). The proof is an explicit computation parallel to the higher-dimensional statement. By the system-of-parameters existence lemma there is g in m making f, g a system of parameters, so that m = sqrt((f, g)); the Noetherian power lemma then gives n with m^n contained in (f, g), and the proof claims N = n + 1 works (proof lines 38122-38127). The verification is a direct ideal computation: for h in m^N one writes h = a f + b g with a and b in m, and the displayed chain (f + h, g) = (f + a f + b g, g) = ((1 + a) f, g) = (f, g) follows because 1 + a is a unit of R, which gives both the system-of-parameters claim and the equality of lengths (proof lines 38128-38134). The non-routine content is the choice N = n + 1 that lets the perturbation be absorbed into the first generator.
